title: observability: automate Prometheus/Grafana + log shipping for Private installs (helm/terraform, dashboards, alerts)
author: Aisha Tan
description:
Motivation: Provide a turnkey observability stack for Redwood Private installs (VPC and on-prem) so customers have a supported Prometheus+Grafana monitoring path and log shipping by default. This PR adds Helm charts and Terraform wiring to provision monitoring components in customer environments, delivers curated Grafana dashboards and alert rules tuned for inference workloads, and introduces upgrade/rollback hooks to make observability upgrades safe during Private installer upgrades.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a new subchart under redwood-private-installer/helm/monitoring that deploys Prometheus Operator (kube-prometheus-stack) with opinionated defaults for token/cost-sensitive inference workloads (reduced retention, scrape interval tuning, remote write optional). 2) Adds a Grafana subchart and a set of JSON dashboards in redwood-private-installer/helm/monitoring/dashboards/* covering routing, per-model latency/cost heatmaps, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates, and ingestion/egress metrics. 3) Adds PrometheusRule alerting definitions tailored to SLOs (high tail latencies, OOMs, long GC pauses, remote write failure). 4) Introduces optional Loki/Promtail pipeline for log shipping with fluent-bit-compatible config and a secure push path for air-gapped installs. 5) Terraform module redwood-terraform/modules/monitoring to provision monitoring network resources (VPC subnets, security groups, IAM roles) and bootstrap Helm releases as part of the private installer flow. 6) Installer hooks: pre-upgrade validation and a rollback-aware Job that snapshots Prometheus data retention settings and restores dashboards on rollback. 7) Docs: updated private-installer/README.md and a new observability.md with configuration guide and runbook for common alerts.

Testing and rollout plan: Unit Helm chart linting and chart-testing were added, integration tests run in the perf-canary k8s cluster that exercises autoscaling and remote-write paths. Terraform module has terratest mocks for VPC networking and an acceptance test that installs the chart into a disposable cluster. Customers can opt-out with install flag monitoring.enabled=false. For managed Dedicated customers the defaults remain unchanged.

Related: ENG-4892 tracks rollout playbook and admin UX, SUP-1124 is the support ticket with a customer requesting turnkey dashboards during their Private deployment.

Notes: The PR intentionally keeps retention defaults conservative to reduce storage costs; customers can override via values.yaml. The Loki pipeline is opt-in when external object storage is configured.
commits_summary: Init monitoring subchart and dashboards; Add terraform monitoring module and bootstrap; Add PrometheusRules and alert templates; Implement installer hooks for upgrade/rollback; Add docs and tests; Fix lint failures from ci run
review_comments: Connor Lee: Left a few nits on the values.yaml defaults—can we reduce scrape_interval for model metrics to 10s for high-qps routes and keep 30s for others?
Aisha Tan (author): Updated values to have per-route scrape_interval override and added documentation in observability.md explaining cost tradeoffs.

Priya Shah: The PrometheusRule for high tail latency looks good, but we should ensure alert flapping is minimized. Suggest adding a 5m for: for_duration and an auto-silence annotation for scheduled maintenance.
Aisha Tan (author): Added for: 5m and maintenance annotations. Also added alert test in perf-canary to ensure we don't get false positives during load tests.
Miguel Ortiz: Terraform module LGTM. One security nit: ensure the IAM role for remote write has least privilege. Added comment and patch applied.
CI Bot: chart-lint passed; integration tests passed on run #3 after fixing RBAC rules.
release_notes: Adds optional observability automation for Private installs: Helm subchart for Prometheus/Grafana and optional Loki pipeline; Terraform module for provisioning monitoring network resources; curated Grafana dashboards for inference workloads; SLO-oriented alert rules; upgrade and rollback hooks to preserve monitoring state. Customers can disable via monitoring.enabled=false.
notes: This PR is the result of cross-team effort between infra, platform, and support. We ran perf-canary scenarios to validate alerting thresholds and kept defaults conservative to avoid storage surprises for Private customers. Follow-up PR will add RBAC-hardening for enterprise compliance.
